# Case Study 1: 1854-Cholera-Outbreak-London (Basic)

**Version:** 2025-06-06  
**Maintained by:** PHI Case Studies Team  
**Contributor:** Jean Baptiste (GitHub user: JKamgang)

---

## About this Digital Case Study

This case study aims to help digital health and public health students and trainees develop geospatial data science skills.

### How to Use This Case Study

This is a **digital case study** built with [Jupyter Notebook](https://jupyter.org/) about the 1854 Cholera Outbreak in London. Dr. John Snow carried out the investigation of this outbreak.

Instead of launching with Binder, this project is designed to be run locally using GitHub and Jupyter Notebook on your desktop.

---

## Requirements

- [GitHub Desktop](https://desktop.github.com/)
- [Jupyter Notebook](https://jupyter.org/install)

---

## Getting Started: Workflow

1. **Fork this repository**  
   - Visit the [GitHub project page](https://github.com/PHI-Case-Studies/1854-Cholera-Outbreak-London-Basic).
   - Click the `Fork` button to create a copy under your GitHub account.

2. **Clone your fork to your local machine**  
   - Open GitHub Desktop.
   - Choose `File > Clone Repository`, then select your forked repository.
   - Choose a local directory to store the project files.

3. **Open the project in Jupyter Notebook**  
   - Launch Jupyter Notebook on your computer.
   - Navigate to the cloned repository folder.
   - Open and run the `.ipynb` notebook files to interact with the case study.
   - Save your work regularly.

4. **Commit and sync your changes**  
   - In GitHub Desktop, write a descriptive commit message.
   - Click `Push origin` to sync changes to your online GitHub fork.

5. **Submit a Pull Request (PR)**  
   - Go to your GitHub fork in a browser.
   - Click `Compare & pull request` to submit your changes for review.
